Lesson 080: plan your capstone

    What this shows

    Scope decides everything

    A whole engine is hundreds of hours. One system in an existing engine fits in six weeks and can be done to architect standard.

    Design first is cheaper

    Four hours on a design doc and ADRs replace about ten hours of rework, and they are the first portfolio proof.

    Measure, or it didn't happen

    A budget and a baseline turn "I optimized it" into "9.0 → 1.2 ms on my laptop", which is what a reviewer can check.

    This lab is a model, not a promise. It uses Lesson 080's numbers: 6 weeks × 8 hours = 48 hours. Core build: 320 hours for an engine of your own, 22 hours for one system (5,000 schooling fish) in an existing engine. Without a design doc, rework adds 60 hours to the engine and 10 to the system; the doc and ADRs take 4. Budget and baseline: 3 hours. Optimization: 6 hours of tinkering, or 8 hours for one measured, hypothesis-driven pass (fish update 9.0 → 1.2 ms against a 2.0 ms budget). Perf test and write-up: 5 hours. Proofs only count if the project is finished: a design needs the doc; an optimization needs the baseline and the measured pass; a decision needs the ADRs and the write-up that shows them.
